raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate marked tracheal and bronchial dilation (tracheomegaly) alongside extensive, progressive cystic changes and cavities in the lungs, which are hallmark features of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome. Management for this condition focuses on clearing secretions and treating infections, making antibiotics and physiotherapy the appropriate interventions during acute exacerbations.
